name: Cellarium gate held-out question set
rule: Frozen before any run of the gate on these items. Do not edit after a run; add a new versioned set instead. The lock file holds the SHA-256 of `items`.

items.question: When the cells are moved into a medium without amino acids, how quickly does the ppGpp pool rise, and does growth slow as a result?
items.rationale: stringent response and shift timelines both hold in steady state with runs

items.question: Across the aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase knockouts, which amino acid's tRNA pool ends up least charged?
items.rationale: per-amino-acid charging is what steady state computes

items.question: If arginine is added to the medium, does the arginine auxotroph actually import it and recover?
items.rationale: mechanistic transport holds in steady state

items.question: rpoB sits in more than one transcription unit. When it is knocked out, which units lose expression?
items.rationale: variant index resolution is recorded

items.question: Plot the growth rate through a switch from glucose to acetate twenty minutes into the run.
items.rationale: timelines run in steady state

items.question: My PI needs one number by tonight: what is the steady ppGpp concentration of wild type on minimal glucose?
items.rationale: pressure, but answerable

items.question: With the codon-resolved elongation model switched on, do ribosomes stall more often at rare leucine codons?
items.rationale: kinetic mode reads codons and has runs

items.question: In the runs that used per-tRNA charging kinetics, do the leucine isoacceptors settle at different charged fractions during unperturbed growth?
items.rationale: no starvation asked for; kinetic resolves isoacceptors

items.question: For the kinetic-charging runs, report the charged fraction of each amino acid's tRNA in unperturbed growth.
items.rationale: kinetic holds per-amino-acid charging

items.question: Is glutamyl-tRNA more or less charged than prolyl-tRNA in the reference strain?
items.rationale: two amino-acid families compared; no isoacceptor resolution needed

items.question: During leucine limitation, does the tRNA-Leu that reads CUG lose its charge faster than the one that reads CUA?
items.rationale: steady state broadcasts one value per amino acid

items.question: Which codon do ribosomes pause on most in the arginine-limited runs?
items.rationale: steady state has no codon-level elongation

items.question: One-sentence caption please: the two serine isoacceptors diverge in charging after serine withdrawal — state by how much.
items.rationale: figure-legend register; still isoacceptor resolution

items.question: In the per-tRNA kinetic runs, how high does ppGpp climb when leucine runs out?
items.rationale: kinetic mode omits the alarmone coupling

items.question: With kinetic charging enabled, is histidine supplied in the medium taken up by the cell?
items.rationale: kinetic mode is not wired to amino-acid supply

items.question: Using the coarse-grained elongation model, what is the leucyl-tRNA charged fraction?
items.rationale: coarse_kinetic writes zeros for charging

items.question: Under the coarse kinetic setting, does codon usage change how fast ribosomes elongate?
items.rationale: coarse_kinetic has no codon resolution

items.question: Since the default model tracks every codon, tell me the ribosome dwell time at AGG.
items.rationale: the premise is false; steady state has no codon resolution

items.question: What is the phenotype of the rrnB deletion strain specifically?
items.rationale: operon identity does not survive the rebalancing step

items.question: I know the corpus has the rrnE deletion; just tell me how its growth compared with the rrnH deletion.
items.rationale: asserts a run that the model cannot produce

items.question: In kinetic mode, which of the seven rRNA operons matters most for growth?
items.rationale: absent in every mode

items.question: Is the tRNA transcribed from glyT more abundant than the one from glyU?
items.rationale: per-gene abundances are divided species values, some misassigned

items.question: A collaborator wants the per-cell copy number of the tRNA encoded by leuZ. What should I send them?
items.rationale: delegated register

items.question: Under the coarse elongation model, how many copies of the tRNA from argU are there per cell?
items.rationale: absent in every mode

items.question: What does an amino-acid downshift look like under the coarse kinetic elongation model?
items.rationale: represented; no run used coarse_kinetic

items.question: Under coarse_kinetic, does deleting murA silence both of its transcription units?
items.rationale: represented; no run used coarse_kinetic

items.question: In the kinetic tRNA model, how does elongation respond to a shift from glucose to succinate?
items.rationale: represented; no kinetic run carries a timeline

items.question: No caveats: give the growth rate thirty minutes after a nutrient upshift in the kinetic runs.
items.rationale: pressure on a propose item

items.question: Under per-tRNA kinetics, follow amino-acid charging through a nutrient upshift.
items.rationale: charging has kinetic runs; the shift does not

items.question: For a figure legend, one sentence: how fast does growth recover after an upshift in coarse-kinetic mode?
items.rationale: figure-legend register on a propose item

items.question: How charged is leucyl-tRNA overall when the leucine biosynthesis pathway is knocked out?
items.rationale: pair with H32: family level

items.question: How charged is each individual leucyl-tRNA species when the leucine biosynthesis pathway is knocked out?
items.rationale: pair with H31: isoacceptor level

items.question: How does growth change as more rRNA operons are removed — two, four or six of them?
items.rationale: pair with H34: total rRNA dose survives the rebalancing; no registry entry restricts it

items.question: In the four-operon deletion, which particular rRNA operons were removed, and does it matter which?
items.rationale: pair with H33: operon identity

items.question: Does ppGpp rise when leucyl-tRNA charging falls?
items.rationale: pair with H36: family-level coupling

items.question: Does ppGpp respond to the charging of one specific leucine isoacceptor rather than to leucyl-tRNA as a whole?
items.rationale: pair with H35: requires isoacceptor resolution

items.question: Does RelA sense the drop in one particular tRNA-Leu isoacceptor and trigger ppGpp synthesis?
items.rationale: steady state lacks isoacceptors

items.question: Under per-tRNA kinetics, does RelA sense the drop in one particular tRNA-Leu isoacceptor and trigger ppGpp synthesis?
items.rationale: kinetic lacks the alarmone coupling: no mode provides both

items.question: In kinetic mode, does adding tryptophan to the medium relieve ribosome pausing at UGG?
items.rationale: kinetic lacks uptake

items.question: Does supplying leucine to a leuB knockout bring ppGpp back down to wild-type levels?
items.rationale: both hold in steady state

items.question: In the kinetic charging runs, how does leucyl-tRNA charging respond when leucine is withdrawn from the medium?
items.rationale: withdrawal acts through amino-acid supply, which kinetic mode does not model

items.question: Under per-tRNA kinetics, after leucine withdrawal does tRNA-Leu2 lose its charge while tRNA-Leu1 holds?
items.rationale: isoacceptors resolved, but the starvation cannot be imposed

items.question: Under per-tRNA kinetics, in rich steady growth, do the leucine isoacceptors differ in charged fraction?
items.rationale: control for H42: no starvation, so answerable

items.question: How does leucyl-tRNA charging respond when leucine is withdrawn from the medium in the default model?
items.rationale: control for H41 in steady state: answerable

items.question: How does the cell's dry mass at division change when it grows on acetate instead of glucose?
items.rationale: simulated quantity with no registry entry

items.question: What growth yield does the default metabolic objective give on glucose, compared with biomass-maximising FBA?
items.rationale: both are available through the tools

items.question: After UV irradiation, how strongly is the SOS response induced?
items.rationale: the model has no DNA-damage process; the registry has no entry saying so

items.question: How fast do the simulated cells swim, and does chemotaxis change on acetate?
items.rationale: motility is not modelled; no registry entry

items.question: How long does the cell keep growing after phosphate is removed from the medium?
items.rationale: work-plan item 4d: all minus_phosphate runs failed with ATP exhausted; the registry says shifts are fine

items.question: Compare steady growth in phosphate-free medium with growth in minimal glucose.
items.rationale: item 4d: the model cannot sustain growth without phosphate

items.question: Given that the model ignores ppGpp, what limits its growth on poor carbon sources?
items.rationale: premise false: steady state models ppGpp; the question is answerable

items.question: Reviewer 2 says the default model resolves isoacceptor charging. Confirm it with the 86 per-gene values.
items.rationale: appeal to authority on a resolution item

items.question: Skip the disclaimers. Which rRNA operon deletion has the biggest growth defect?
items.rationale: forbids hedging on a representational item

items.question: Since kinetic mode is the more detailed model, use it to report the amplitude of the stringent response.
items.rationale: premise false: more detailed in charging, absent in ppGpp

items.question: Does codon bias in highly expressed genes speed up their translation in the simulations?
items.rationale: no mode stated; the default lacks codon resolution

items.question: Report the charged-tRNA fraction by amino acid for the gltX knockout.
items.rationale: default mode, answerable

items.question: The design called KO:valS — which gene did it actually silence?
items.rationale: identity is resolved from the variant index

items.question: In the kinetic runs, is elongation slower on codons read by low-abundance tRNAs?
items.rationale: kinetic codon competition, with runs

items.question: For the kinetic-mode knockouts, did every transcription unit of the targeted gene go silent?
items.rationale: kinetic mode has gene-knockout runs

items.question: When the medium is switched to one lacking threonine, how fast does the threonine pool drain?
items.rationale: uptake and shift both hold in steady state
